subject: \$! snapshots instead of aliasing — $! needs the $./$| magic-cell box (blocks op/bless.t + uni/bless.t t81)
description:
`\$!` captures the CURRENT VALUE instead of aliasing the magic variable.

  $! = 1; my $string = "$!";
  $! = 2;  my $f1 = \$!;  $! = 1;
  print ${$f1};        # perl: "Operation not permitted" (live)
                       # PCL:  "No such file or directory" (snapshot at \ time)

Control passes: `\$plain` aliases correctly.

ROOT: `$!` is ACCESSOR-based, not box-based. Emission:
  read   $!        ->  (p-errno-string)
  write  $! = 1    ->  (p-setf (p-errno-string) 1)
  ref    \$!       ->  (p-backslash (p-errno-string))   <-- refs the VALUE
So the snapshot is structural: there is no cell to point at.

THE MECHANISM TO REUSE ALREADY EXISTS. `p-magic-cell` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:991) is a scalar lvalue with getter/setter closures, intercepted at the unbox/box-set chokepoints, and `$.` (line 1063) and `$|` (1089) are already defined as `(defvar |$X| (make-p-box (make-p-magic-cell :getter … :setter …)))`. Giving `$!` the same shape makes `\$!` a ref to a real cell and deref reads live, with no new machinery.

WHY NOT DONE IN THE R1 WINDOW: `$!` is read in essentially every error path (`open … or die $!`), so switching its emission from an accessor call to a box touches codegen, every read/write site, AND the existing `local $!` special case (which binds *p-stored-errno* — Pl/Parser.pm's local handler has a dedicated branch). Blast radius is far larger than the one test it fixes.

BLOCKS: op/bless.t t81 and uni/bless.t t81 (same root — "ref is ref to magic": `$f1 = bless \$!, "F"` then checking `${$_[0]}` reads the CURRENT $!). Both files are otherwise 1-2 failures from green.

Probes: scratchpad w0/r2.pl (alias vs snapshot + plain-var control), r3.pl/r4.pl (emission).</description>
